interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is documented. Positive surgical margins is reported absent. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 40.84 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 32.67–49.01 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Favorable findings include negative surgical margins and the absence of seminal vesicle invasion and lymph node metastasis, which are positive prognostic indicators. Conversely, the preoperative PSA of 6.2 and the pathological T3a stage contribute to increased risk. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy difference is noted, as the biopsy report lacks Gleason pattern and ISUP grading, which introduces uncertainty regarding the true tumor aggressiveness. Missing nodal sampling, although nodes were sampled, widens the uncertainty regarding complete nodal status. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are critical unknowns that would significantly revise this prognosis. The current horizon suggests a follow-up period of 40.83884626783468 months without an observed event.

attempts.text: The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage of pT3a, presence of extraprostatic extension, negative surgical margins, and no invasion of the seminal vesicles. Lymphovascular invasion was absent, and there was no lymph node metastasis documented. The preoperative PSA was 6.2. The surgical findings, including "surgical margins were negative" and "there was no lymph node metastasis," are favorable prognostic factors. Conversely, the preoperative PSA of 6.2 is a factor influencing risk. The biopsy information is incomplete, as the "Gleason pattern and ISUP report missing." The nodal status is documented as no lymph node metastasis, although "Missing nodal sampling, although nodes were sampled, widens the uncertainty regarding complete nodal status." The prognosis is guided by the expert horizon, which indicates a numeric horizon of 40.83884626783468 months to recurrence. Information that would revise this prognosis, particularly the postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory, is currently absent.
